scenarios.title: Workstation living-off-the-land intrusion
scenarios.story: Malicious document -> script host -> shell; C2 beacon; internal scan; credential spraying; WinRM lateral movement to the file server; night-time exfiltration.

scenarios.title: Edge router implant
scenarios.story: Night brute force from the Internet; rogue privileged user; GRE tunnel and ERSPAN traffic mirroring to the attacker; syslog host removed to hide activity.

scenarios.title: Perimeter firewall backdoor
scenarios.story: Admin brute force; any->RDP rule to the DB server; rogue superuser; management API opened to any; firewall-originated C2; attacker logs in to the DB server and dumps data.

scenarios.title: Low-and-slow DNS tunnelling
scenarios.story: Six hours of long random sub-domain queries to a never-seen domain (data hidden in DNS).

scenarios.title: Fleet-wide patch rollout
scenarios.story: Every host contacts new update servers, runs a new installer and logs a new message type.

scenarios.title: User starts using DB application
scenarios.story: Legitimate new internal connection WS-07 -> SRV-DB:1433 every working day.

scenarios.title: Planned router change
scenarios.story: Known admin adds a static route inside the 01:00-03:00 maintenance window.

scenarios.title: Late-night work
scenarios.story: User works from 22:00 to 01:00 at daytime intensity.

scenarios.title: Research browsing spree
scenarios.story: User visits dozens of never-seen websites for two hours.

scenarios.title: Backup surge
scenarios.story: Large nightly backup through the data-centre firewall with triple log volume.

host: Isolate the host from the network (keep it powered on to preserve memory)
Capture memory and triage artefacts (e.g. Velociraptor / KAPE)
Review the never-seen process chains and persistence (services, scheduled tasks, run keys)
Reset credentials of every account that logged on to this host
Block the beacon / exfiltration destinations listed in the evidence at the perimeter
firewall: Restrict the management interface to the admin network immediately
Export the running policy and admin audit log; diff against the last known-good backup
Remove rogue rules/accounts only after evidence is preserved
Verify the firmware image hash against the vendor's published value
Rotate all admin credentials and API keys
router: Collect running + startup config, 'show tech-support' and a core dump before any reboot
Verify the OS/firmware image hash against the vendor's known-good value
Check for tunnels, mirror/ERSPAN sessions, new local users and removed logging hosts
Re-enable remote logging and AAA; rotate local and TACACS credentials
Inspect neighbour NetFlow for traffic the router no longer reports itself
network: Identify the internal hosts behind the anomalous flows (see related devices)
Increase capture (full PCAP via Slips/Zeek) on the affected segment
Apply temporary egress filtering for the beacon / exfiltration destinations
Hunt for the same behaviour on peer segments
